translated_text: May 19, 1940. I received two letters from you, my little one. After that, I have some at home. It's Sunday, but there are no more Sundays where we live. We work every day. My little one, I'm sending you 400 francs because I received money for the paper and I don't want to leave that money here. I have enough, and if I need anything, you know I won't ask. I don't want to keep a lot of money here. When we return here, I can't say. For the moment, certainly. I think there are no changes. But we don't know anything. Your morals are very good and suit us better than ever. The Yugoslavian newspaper gave me great pleasure. It's only a small thing, but better than nothing. - Every time. It's wonderful that you feel quite well, my darling. Is the baby brave? - You already received Madly's letter. If not, a good one. It's very important, my little one. You mustn't do anything silly. 'My darling, I'm so happy with you and your letters, you don't know that. Lots of love from your Bob D'INF. Mrs. F 131 19 ERA 5 E.
